t: This is Wheatsheaf Hall in Vauxhall, south London, a former Congregational Church mission hall. It's a grade two listed building and is now a community centre. It was designed by Robert Williams, a Welsh architect and social campaigner who lived from 1848 to 1918. Williams studied architecture in London and set up his practice here in 1887. His work showed a Gothic Revival influence. Later, from 1914, he practised in Egypt, where he built Cairo's largest shop. This hall is one of his London buildings.
